studies.title: Investigation the effects of obstacle geometries and injection molding parameters on weld line strength using experimental and finite element methods in plastic injection molding
studies.journal: International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer
studies.materialContext: Polypropylene specimens moulded with intentionally generated weld lines and comparison geometries.
studies.toolContext: Experimental mould incorporated obstacles with different edge angles to generate controlled weld-line conditions; specimens were produced on a Mitsubishi 50 MetIII injection-moulding machine.
physicalQualityOutcomes: comparison of specimens with and without weld lines
studies.supports: Weld-line geometry and moulding conditions measurably change tensile and impact performance of injection-moulded polypropylene, demonstrating that weld-line structural risk requires mechanical evidence rather than appearance alone.
studies.limitation: The polypropylene grade, obstacle geometries, machine, tensile/impact methods and tested process window are experiment-specific; the measured parameter effects and numerical strengths are not universal weld-line acceptance limits or process settings.

studies.title: On the assessment of strength and durability of weld lines in injection-moulded unreinforced and short glass fiber reinforced polypropylene
authors: Sten J. J. van den Broek
studies.materialContext: Unreinforced isotactic polypropylene and 30% short-glass-fibre-reinforced iPP injection-moulded into specimens containing a central weld line.
studies.toolContext: Injection-moulded tensile specimens with a central stagnating-flow weld line; short- and long-term mechanical tests were performed across temperature and loading-rate conditions.
physicalQualityOutcomes: short-term weld-line tensile strength and failure mode
crack-growth behaviour and ductile-to-brittle failure transition
studies.supports: Weld-line mechanical performance is loading-, temperature-, material- and time-dependent; short-term visual or tensile evidence alone can miss durability and crack-growth risks.
studies.limitation: The unreinforced and 30% short-glass-fibre iPP materials, weld geometry and mechanical loading programme are specific to the experiment; the reported strength transitions and test rates do not define universal weld-line thresholds.

supportingStudy.title: Comparative study of weld-line strength for unfilled and glass-filled thermoplastic polyamide-6 materials
supportingStudy.use: Supporting material/reinforcement evidence comparing tensile properties of moulded plaques with and without weld lines; not required for the two-study minimum.
supportingStudy.limitation: The tested unfilled, 30% glass-filled and 50% glass-filled PA6 materials and plaque geometry do not define universal weld-line strength-reduction factors.

promotionClaim: Promote the mechanism-level statement that measured weld-line structural performance depends on material, reinforcement, flow/weld geometry, thermal/process history and service loading, and that visual appearance alone is insufficient; mechanical testing and physical part-quality outcomes are required when structural integrity matters. Do not promote any reported tensile strength, impact strength, test rate, temperature, pressure or processing condition as a universal setting, acceptance limit or guaranteed root-cause threshold.
